text:
Alex: kicking off a thread for the new trace-simulator parity run. goal: apples-to-apples comparison vs prod serving for kernel selection + kv cache behavior.
Maria: high level plan?
Alex: 1) anonymize traces with the new salted-hash mapper 2) reservoir-sample sessions (1% stratified by seq_len) 3) run simulator with deterministic seeds and kernel-selection-forcing flags 4) compare token-level outputs and perf counters to prod logs.
Sam: for anonymization we used sha256(salt + session_id) -> 64b hex, then map to bucket ids. that keeps distribution but strips PII. anyone object?
Jordan: that sounds fine. ensure we persist the salt in Vault so runs are repeatable.
Taylor: note: the old anonymizer also truncated user messages; new one preserves token counts which matters for batching heuristics.
Alex: good point. we need preserved lengths for batching sims.
Maria: sampling detail: reservoir sampling per 1-hour window, cap 10k sessions. implemented as: ````python
# pseudo
for window in windows:
  sample = reservoir_sample(stream(window), k=10000, seed=42)
````
Sam: also stratify by model and region to avoid regional kernel bias.
Alex: instrumentation: enable profiler flags `--emit-kernel-log` and `--kv-warmup-trace` so we capture kernel choices and kv-cache hit/warmup counters (cold vs warmed). replay-bot: run queued: trace-sim v3 on s3://traces/2026-03-12/ -> started.
replay-bot: job 78921 logs: https://internal.corp/jobs/78921/logs (link)
Jordan: quick gotcha: the prod runtime has a non-deterministic kernel fallback path when a kernel OOMs. we need to force `--disable-fallback` during parity checks so we see mismatch causes rather than silent fallbacks.
Taylor: agreed. Also set `--max-batch-ms=8` to match production batching latency SLO for this run.
Alex: running simulator command posted to reproduce: ````bash
./trace-sim --trace s3://anon/traces/2026-03-12/sample-1k.json \
  --anon-salt ${VAULT_SALT} \
  --seed 98765 \
  --force-kernel "cuda_gelu_optv2" \
  --disable-fallback \
  --emit-kernel-log \
  --kv-warmup-trace \
  --max-batch-ms 8 \
  --output ./out/parity-run-1932156789.json
````
Maria: initial quick diff: token outputs matched for 87% of tokens, but mismatches cluster at long history shots where kv-cache warmup decreased early token latency in prod.
Sam: mismatch pattern: simulator used different KV eviction ordering leading to different KV hits at step ~120 for session X. We logged kv events: ``kv_event(session=0, step=119, evicted_key=abc123)`` vs prod: ``kv_hit(session=0, step=119, key=abc123)``
Jordan: that sounds like nondeterministic hash ordering in our LRU bucket map. we should enable `--stable-kv-ordering` to force deterministic bucket scans.
Taylor: also check that quantization kernel selection is identical: production on that node used `int8-qkv` kernel for qk matmul when seq_len>1024; simulator had a length threshold bug that flipped at 1023. off-by-one.
Alex: good catch. We'll patch simulator threshold and re-run.
Maria: expected re-run plan: patch threshold, enable `--stable-kv-ordering`, re-run same sample with same seed + `--collect-diffs=token,pos` to get minimal repro slices.
Sam: we should also capture perf counters (cycles per token) and kernel timings so we can attribute latency differences to kernel vs kv behavior. add `--perf-counters=kernel_ms,kv_ms,cpu_ms`.
Jordan: note for the record: anonymity preserved (checked top-10 hashed ids are stable, no raw contents in artifacts).
Alex: next steps: Sam to run patched sim and attach diff slices; Maria to prepare short runbook for running parity checks (steps + flags); Jordan to add a unit test for kv ordering; Taylor to open a small PR for the length threshold.
Taylor: I'll open PR now with test vectors.
Sam: kicked off re-run job 78946. replay-bot: job 78946 queued. :thumbsup:
Alex: thanks team — let's aim to have reproducible parity or clear list of divergence causes by EOD tomorrow.
Maria: sounds good. if run produces >1% token mismatch we'll escalate to perf-incident with kernel owners.
Alex: adding note: when we report apples-to-apples numbers, include batch-size distribution histogram, median sequence length, and kv-warmup fraction (pct tokens with warm KV). helps isolate root cause.
Jordan: leaving link to diff tool: https://internal.tools/diffviz with params `--key token_pos --threshold 0`
Taylor: ping me if you want me to re-run with a smaller seed set for quicker iterate.
Alex: closing for now. will post results when job 78946 finishes.
